question: In December 2024, the Union Health Minister said that the TB incidence rate in India has decline to __________ per 100000 population in 2023.
solution:
The correct answer is __**195 per 100,000 population**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• In December 2024, the Union Health Minister announced that the **Tuberculosis (TB) incidence rate** in India had declined to **195 per 100,000 population** in 2023. 
• This decline reflects the success of the government’s initiatives under the **National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP)**. 
• The **World Health Organization (WHO)** had earlier estimated India's TB incidence rate for 2021 as **210 per 100,000 population**, showcasing a significant improvement in disease control efforts. 
• The reduction aligns with India’s commitment to achieve the **United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)** and eliminate TB by **2025**, five years ahead of the global target. 
• Various initiatives like the **“Nikshay Poshan Yojana”** (nutritional support for TB patients) and the **introduction of new diagnostic tools** have contributed to this progress. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Tuberculosis (TB):** 
• **TB** is a contagious disease caused by the bacteria *Mycobacterium tuberculosis*. 
• It primarily affects the lungs but can also impact other parts of the body, such as the spine, brain, and kidneys. 
• The disease spreads through the air when people with active TB in their lungs cough, sneeze, or spit. 
• **National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP):** 
• Previously known as the Revised National Tuberculosis Control Programme (RNTCP), it was renamed in **2020** to reflect India’s commitment to eliminating TB. 
• NTEP aims to eliminate TB in India by **2025** through early diagnosis, treatment, and care for patients. 
• Key components include free diagnostic services, drug delivery, and nutritional support through the **Nikshay Poshan Yojana.** 
• **WHO Global TB Report:** 
• The **World Health Organization (WHO)** releases an annual Global TB Report to track progress in eliminating TB worldwide. 
• As per the 2022 report, India accounted for **26%** of the global TB burden, but significant strides have been made in reducing the incidence rate. 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):** 
• The **SDG 3** aims to ensure healthy lives and promote well-being for all ages, including ending the epidemics of TB by **2030**. 
• India has advanced its target to eliminate TB by **2025**, showing strong political commitment and implementation of health programs. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Nikshay Poshan Yojana:** 
• Launched in **2018**, this scheme provides **₹500 per month** to TB patients for nutritional support during their treatment. 
• The funds are directly transferred to patients' bank accounts under the **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)** system. 
• **Advanced Diagnostic Tools for TB:** 
• India has adopted modern diagnostic techniques like **CB-NAAT (Cartridge-Based Nucleic Acid Amplification Test)** and **TrueNat** to detect TB and drug-resistant TB quickly and accurately. 
• These tools have improved early detection rates, helping to reduce TB transmission. 
• **Patient-Centric Care:** 
• Under the NTEP, patients receive **free access to TB drugs and treatment**, including for multi-drug resistant TB (MDR-TB). 
• Community engagement and awareness campaigns have been crucial in reducing the stigma associated with TB.
